title: Regional failover gatekeeper: capacity-aware rate controller and soft geo-affinity
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Summary: Build a 'Regional Failover Gatekeeper' component in the request director that enforces latency-first routing while respecting region capacity, providing soft geo-affinity, and driving graceful load shedding and circuit-breaker behavior. The goal is to keep percentiles under SLOs during regional capacity pressure and partial outages while minimizing cross-region latency regressions and customer error rates.

Motivation: Current routing is either strict geo-pin (which overloads local hotspots) or best-effort latency route (which causes excessive cross-region traffic and cold-cache regressions). We need a middle ground: prefer local region for affinity, but allow controlled overflow with capacity-aware tokens and circuit-breaker protections. This will reduce SLO violations and tail latencies for the majority of traffic while providing predictable behavior during spikes and region-level incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Director exposes new routing mode 'gatekeeper' behind feature flag
95th-token-latency across representative workload does not increase by >5% in normal traffic compared to baseline
During simulated 30% regional capacity loss, global error-rate increase limited to <1.5x baseline and cross-region tail latency increase limited to <20% for overflowed requests
Circuit-breaker trips per-region are recorded, and requests rerouted to fallback regions as expected
Observability: dashboards for gatekeeper decisions (per-request reason code), token-bucket fill rates, circuit-breaker state, and per-region SLO compliance
E2E canary rollout to 5% traffic with metrics alarms and automated rollback on elevated error or latency signals
design_notes:
Core concepts: 
- Soft geo-affinity: requests carry a small affinity token (TTL configurable, default 5 minutes) that biases routing to the origin region but expires to avoid hot-spot persistence.
- Capacity-aware rate controller: each destination region exposes a token-bucket shaped capacity hint (tokens per-second + burst). The director consumes tokens for overflowed requests; when depleted, director will progressively shed or redirect based on policy.
- Latency-first selector with cost for cross-region: base latency score + affinity bonus + capacity-penalty. Score formula is tunable via config.
- Circuit-breaker: per-region SLA windowed circuit-breakers that open when error-rate or queue latency exceed thresholds for N windows. Opened breakers redirect to secondary region or fallback model with reduced cost.
- Load shedding policy: graceful shedding tiers (background batch jobs, low-priority tokenization tasks, then live generation); last resort is 429 with deterministic Retry-After and client hints.
- Backpressure signals: integrate autoscaler signals from Dedicated pools and capacity estimator from runtime to seed token-bucket rates.

Data model: minimal per-request metadata (origin-region, affinity-token-id, requested-model-hash, priority-class). State kept in memory for fast paths; persistent counters emitted to metrics for debugging.

Operational knobs: per-customer and global caps, per-region weights, affinity TTL, token refill rate, breaker thresholds, prioritization of model variants.
implementation_plan:
Milestones: 
1) Prototype gatekeeper scoring in director (feature-flagged, non-blocking) — implement scoring function and affinity token plumbing. Owner: Claire. (2w)
2) Capacity hint API between runtime and director, token-bucket implementation in director with per-region metrics. Owner: Samir Patel. (2w)
3) Circuit-breaker state machine and fallback routing rules; integrate with rollout engine for canary. Owner: Priya Kapoor. (1w)
4) Load-shedding policy implementation and fallthrough ordering; deterministic 429 responses and client hints. Owner: Michael O'Connor. (1w)
5) Observability: dashboards, per-request logging (reason codes), alerts on deviation from SLOs. Owner: Diego Alvarez + Reliability team. (1w)
6) Chaos and perf testing, canary rollout, post-canary monitoring and gradual ramp. Owner: Claire + QA. (2w)

Feature flags: director.gatekeeper.enabled, director.gatekeeper.affinity_ttl, director.gatekeeper.token_bucket_enabled, director.gatekeeper.breaker_thresholds.

Security: feature requires security review because routing decisions touch tenancy and could reveal topology-state; ensure no PII in reason codes and that affinity tokens are opaque and short-lived.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for scoring and token-bucket logic. Integration test harness with local multi-region runtime emulation. Load tests with synthetic workloads (chat streaming and embedding bursts) to measure token consumption and tail latency. Chaos experiments: region partition, partial GPU degradation, and autoscaler delays. Canary: deploy to 5% traffic with additional debug logging sampling, run for 72 hours with SLO monitors. Performance targets: no more than 5% median increase and <10% p95 increase for primary customers in non-failure scenarios.

Failure modes to test explicitly: 
- Token bucket depletion: verify shedding and correct Retry-After header generation
- Breaker flapping: ensure hysteresis prevents oscillation
- Affinity token hot-spot: ensure TTL expiry and adaptive decay prevent persistent overload
- Observability gaps: ensure every routed request emits decision reason metric for postmortem
rollout_and_rollback:
Rollout: gated by feature flag and canary job. Start at 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring windows. Each stage requires 24-72 hour verification and automatic rollback if: error-rate > 1.5x baseline OR p95 latency > threshold for two consecutive windows.

Rollback: flip director.gatekeeper.enabled -> false (fast path), revert any runtime capacity hint schema if needed, flush in-memory affinity caches. Revert commits if root cause traced to new logic. Post-rollback: run incident postmortem and revert thresholds.
open_questions: Affinity token TTL: default 5 minutes — acceptable tradeoff between locality and fairness?
Fallback ordering: should we prefer proximal cold-cache regions over remote warm-cache regions? (tradeoff between latency and model quality)
Per-customer quotas: should customer-specific token buckets be enforced in gatekeeper or upstream quota layer?
Telemetry costs: sampling rate for per-request decision logging must balance observability and cost

2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez: Observability proposal added to dashboard link. Recommend sampling 1% of requests for detailed debug logs during canary and 0.1% in prod.
Action: QA to prepare chaos scenarios for next week.

2026-03-13 Claire Zhang: Load test (5k rps) with synthetic chat workload: token bucket behavior matches expectation; when one region reduced to 50% capacity, overflow traffic increased cross-region by 12% and p95 rose by 9% in overflowed requests. This meets intermediate acceptance criteria; preparing canary plan.
